headline: Revenue grows, but acquisition charges drive a steep loss
summary_short: Gilead's Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% y/y to $7.8B on HIV and oncology strength, but a GAAP net loss of $(10.5)B and diluted EPS of $(8.45) resulted from $11.2B of acquired IPR&D expense tied to the Arcellx, Tubulis and Ouro Medicines deals plus a $1.75B Immunomedics impairment; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $(6.75).
summary_long: Total revenue grew 10% y/y to $7.8B (product sales ex-Veklury +10% to $7.6B), led by HIV (+12% y/y to $5.7B, Biktarvy +7% to $3.8B, Descovy +48% to $967M) and Trodelvy (+26% to $457M), partly offset by Veklury (-81%) and Cell Therapy (-14%). GAAP operating income swung to a $(10.4)B loss and net income to $(10.5)B, driven by $11.2B of acquired IPR&D expense from the Arcellx, Tubulis, and Ouro Medicines acquisitions plus a $1.75B Immunomedics IPR&D impairment; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $(6.75). Cash fell to $3.2B from $10.6B at year-end on $11.3B of acquisition outflows, $2.8B debt repayment, and $2.1B dividends. Gilead raised full-year product-sales guidance to $30.1-30.4B but widened GAAP/non-GAAP loss-per-share guidance to $(3.75)-$(3.40) and $(0.65)-$(0.30) on the IPR&D charge.

drivers.explanation: CEO Daniel O'Day called the base business "very strong" with 10% y/y revenue growth led by HIV, Trodelvy and Livdelzi, but the GAAP bottom line swung to a large loss on acquisition-related IPR&D charges.
Growth was driven by higher HIV sales, Trodelvy and Livdelzi, and higher royalty/contract revenue from a prior IP sale, partly offset by lower Veklury and Cell Therapy/HCV sales.
Product gross margin held roughly flat (79.3% vs 78.7% y/y); the absolute cost increase tracks higher product sales volume rather than a margin deterioration.

Swung to a loss on $11.2B of acquired IPR&D expense (Arcellx, Tubulis, Ouro Medicines, net of the Lakefront collaboration) plus a $1.75B IPR&D impairment tied to prior Immunomedics assets and higher integration-related opex.
Tracks the operating-income swing to a loss; partly offset by higher other income, including higher net gains on equity securities, versus the prior period.
Tracks the pretax swing; partly offset by a lower income tax expense ($242M vs $468M y/y) since the acquired IPR&D charges are largely non-deductible, pushing the effective tax rate negative.

Decline was primarily driven by the $(9.08)-per-share impact of acquired IPR&D and related tax expenses from the Arcellx, Tubulis and Ouro Medicines deals, plus the Immunomedics impairment and higher opex, partly offset by higher revenue and lower tax.
Same $(9.08)-per-share acquired-IPR&D and tax impact as basic EPS, with a near-identical diluted share count offering no meaningful offset.

First-half cash outflows of $11.3B for acquisitions, $2.8B of debt repayments and $2.1B of dividends outweighed $6.1B of operating cash flow and $4.1B of new debt proceeds; figure is YTD, not quarter-isolated.
Gilead issued $3.0B of senior unsecured notes and borrowed $1.1B under a one-year term loan facility, primarily to help fund the quarter's acquisitions.
Not explained in the release; the q/q rise likely reflects debt nearing maturity reclassifying to current, but no specific maturity detail is given.
The $11.7B q/q equity decline is arithmetically consistent with the quarter's $10.5B net loss plus dividends paid, only partly offset by other comprehensive items.
Modest decline reflects the $355M of common stock repurchased in the quarter, part of $774M repurchased year-to-date.
